difficulty_notes: The main structural challenge is that the user's turn 3 is a pure constraint-provision message — it surfaces no new intent dimension beyond what was already in the tree, but it does instantiate the planning context concretely. Grouping the five input pieces (task list, meetings, hours, energy, urgency) into one 'Concrete daily task list with constraints' node with report urgency as a child is a defensible compression because the pieces collectively serve one function: grounding the schedule. Separating all five into sibling nodes would produce a flat list of inputs rather than a meaningful intent hierarchy. The meta tree is unambiguous: the user's request for a planner-ready checklist is a format/style preference that does not affect any content node and clearly passes the independence test. Break scheduling (n3) was articulated at turn 1 and then the specific break suggestions were affirmed at turn 5 — this is one node confirmed rather than two; no duplicate was created. The absence of any engagement with the style options (strict / flexible / gentle / efficiency-focused) offered at turn 2 is noted; no emerging node was created for absence of preference.
validation_check: The extracted root structure — a planning tree rooted in workday organisation with sub-nodes for prioritisation, break scheduling, realistic goal-setting, stress reduction, a concrete task list, report urgency, minimum-success planning, and a checklist output — maps closely to the stated task expectation, which explicitly named prioritisation, realistic time-blocking, break suggestions, a minimum-success plan, and a clear actionable checklist. All five elements from the task expectation are represented in the tree or adopted immediately in the surfacing log. The meta tree captures the planner-format preference the task expectation also anticipated. There are no significant mismatches.
